args.description: Password-reset and verification mails allowed per address per hour

args.description: A session ends after this long without a request

args.description: A session ends this long after sign-in, however active it is

args.name: license_key_file

args.description: Google OAuth client id. Set with GRUND_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET

args.name: capacity_token

args.name: relay_address

args.description: The relay's URL as machines reach it, e.g. https://relay.example.com. Registration tells machines this URL. Plain http only for loopback
args.name: relay_url

args.description: The relay's certificate chain (PEM). Without it the relay listens in plain HTTP, for a proxy in front that terminates TLS and passes the WebSocket upgrade through
args.name: relay_tls_cert_file

args.description: The private key of GRUND_RELAY_TLS_CERT_FILE (PEM)

args.name: app_domain

args.name: edges

args.name: domain

args.description: Where HTTPS listens. ACME's TLS-ALPN-01 challenge is answered here, so for ACME this must be what port 443 of GRUND_DOMAIN reaches
args.name: tls_listen

args.description: A plain-http listener, e.g. 0.0.0.0:80, that redirects every request to GRUND_PUBLIC_URL and answers ACME's HTTP-01 challenge. Needed for GRUND_ACME_CHALLENGE=http-01. Off by default: TLS-ALPN-01 needs no port 80
args.name: tls_redirect_listen

args.description: A certificate chain (PEM, leaf first) to serve instead of ordering one. Re-read when the file changes, so a renewal by another tool is picked up. Set with GRUND_TLS_KEY_FILE
args.name: tls_cert_file

args.description: The private key of GRUND_TLS_CERT_FILE (PEM)
args.name: tls_key_file

args.description: The ACME directory certificates are ordered from, e.g. https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory: GRUND_DOMAIN's, and those of `grund relay`s on other hosts (grund.certificates.v1), which is why it may be set without GRUND_DOMAIN. args.description: A contact address for the ACME account, e.g. ops@example.com. Optional: Let's Encrypt no longer mails about expiry
args.name: acme_contact

args.description: A PEM file of extra roots to trust for GRUND_ACME_DIRECTORY's own HTTPS, for a private or test CA (step-ca, Pebble). Public CAs need none
args.name: acme_ca_file

args.description: The ACME profile named on every order. Let's Encrypt's `classic` is 90 days today (64 from 2027-02-10, 45 from 2028-02-16); renewal follows the CA's renewal information, so a lifetime change needs no configuration change
args.name: acme_profile

args.description: How the CA checks this instance holds GRUND_DOMAIN: tls-alpn-01 on GRUND_TLS_LISTEN (no port 80 needed), or http-01 on GRUND_TLS_REDIRECT_LISTEN
args.name: acme_challenge

args.description: The first wait after a failed order, in seconds; each further failure doubles it, up to 12 hours, and a CA's Retry-After is waited out when it asks for longer. 300 keeps a broken setup inside Let's Encrypt's 5 failed validations per name per hour. Lower only against a test CA

args.description: How often each replica looks for a renewed certificate (in the database, or GRUND_TLS_CERT_FILE's modification time), and for due ACME work

args.name: vm_rootfs_sha256

conventions.confirmation: Commands marked destructive ask on a terminal, and need --yes when stdin or stderr is not one, or with --output json.
conventions.credentials: GRUND_TOKEN (a personal access token, grund_pat_…) and GRUND_INSTANCE, else the credentials file grund login writes (mode 0600; GRUND_CREDENTIALS_FILE, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/grund/credentials.yaml).
conventions.dry_run: --dry-run prints grund.cli.v1.DryRun (apps deploy: grund.cli.v1.DeployResult with dryRun set) and changes nothing. A release's dry run is checked by the instance as a deploy is.
conventions.errors: A failed command prints grund.cli.v1.ErrorOutput on stderr with --output json, and exits with its code's status.
conventions.organisation: --org, else GRUND_ORG, else grund orgs use, else the token's organisation, else the account's only one.
conventions.output: --output json (or --json, or GRUND_OUTPUT=json) prints one JSON document on stdout: the protobuf JSON of the message the command's output names. Fields at their default may be absent. 64-bit integers are strings.

exit_codes.meaning: The command line is wrong: an unknown flag, a missing argument or a bad value.
A destructive command needs --yes when nobody can be asked.
More than one organisation could be meant: pass --org or run grund orgs use.
No credential: run grund login, or set GRUND_TOKEN and GRUND_INSTANCE.
The instance refused the credential: unknown, revoked or expired.
The credential may not do this: the role, or the token's scope.
No such organisation, app, release, machine, domain, member or token, or not one the credential reaches.
The current state refuses it: a name taken, a limit reached, a rollout halted.
The instance refused the input; field names it when known.
The instance could not be reached or could not answer now; retrying may work.
With --wait: the release did not go live.
